cards.text: The prophet Jeremiah gets a word from the LORD for all the people of Judah, in the fourth year of Jehoiakim, king of Judah. That's also year one for Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, and friend, when the Bible starts telling time by BABYLON'S calendar, pull up a chair. Jeremiah speaks to all of Judah and everyone living in Jerusalem.

Jeremiah opens with the math: the LORD's word has been coming to him since the thirteenth year of Josiah, the current king's DAD, right up to this very day. Friend, that's not a sermon intro, that's a RECEIPT.

cards.question: Jeremiah has been speaking the LORD's word to Judah again and again for ___ years.
All those years of Jeremiah speaking to Judah again and again. How have the people responded?

cards.text: It's not just Jeremiah, either: the LORD has sent ALL His servants the prophets to them, again and again. That's the same message from every single person in the group chat.

cards.question: Jeremiah says the people of Judah listened to the other prophets the LORD sent, just not to him.

cards.text: The prophets' message fits on one recipe card: turn now, each of you, from your evil ways and deeds. Friend, I've burnt cookies following WAY harder instructions than that.

cards.question: If the people turned from their evil ways, the prophets said they could stay in the ___ the LORD gave them and their fathers, forever.
Along with turning from their evil ways, the prophets gave the people of Judah another warning. What was it?

answers.text: Do not go down to Egypt

cards.text: And the prophets passed along the LORD's promise: 'Then I will do you no harm.' Friend, that deal's so good I'd have signed it with my MUSTACHE.
But the LORD says they didn't listen, and it's to their own harm. It's an oven timer beeping again and again while the whole kitchen yells, "FIVE more minutes!"

cards.question: The LORD says the people of Judah provoked Him to anger with what?

cards.text: Twenty-three years of warnings, and now Jeremiah gets to the "therefore." The LORD of Hosts says, 'Because you have not obeyed My words,' and then He says what He will do.

cards.question: Because Judah has not obeyed, who does the LORD say He will send for?
In this message, the LORD calls Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon 'My servant.'

cards.text: My SERVANT. Nebuchadnezzar, king of BABYLON, along with all the families of the north. I bet nobody in Jerusalem saw that word coming.

cards.question: Who does the LORD say He will bring Nebuchadnezzar against?

answers.text: This land and the nations around it
Sheba and the far lands of the south

cards.text: An object of horror and contempt, an EVERLASTING desolation: friend, the LORD is not whispering here. Then He gets specific about what He'll take away from them.

cards.question: Which of these does the LORD say He will banish from the land?

answers.text: The voices of the bride and bridegroom
The sound of the war trumpets
The tramp of the marching armies

cards.text: No sounds of joy, no millstones grinding, no light of the lamp. I know dark from my years in the junk drawer, friend, but this is a whole land becoming a desolate wasteland.

cards.question: The LORD says these nations will serve the king of Babylon for ___ years.

cards.text: Seventy years serving the same boss. That's a whole career with ZERO vacation days, but when those seventy years are complete, the LORD has a word about Babylon itself.

cards.question: When the seventy years are complete, what will the LORD do to the king of Babylon and his nation?
The LORD says the land of the Chaldeans, Babylon's own land, will become an everlasting desolation too.

cards.text: The LORD says He'll bring on that land every word He's spoken against it, everything written in this book, which Jeremiah prophesied against all the nations. Babylon's been the big boss this whole time, and now the big boss is getting WRITTEN UP.

cards.question: Many nations and great kings will enslave Babylon, and the LORD will repay them according to their ___ and the work of their hands.
